invalid.claim: B is buying multiple items at a cosmetics store

decisions.claim: B said they were only going to get a few things
decisions.reason: A's statement 'I thought you said you were only going to get a few things' presupposes B previously made this claim. The 'I thought you said' construction is a well-grounded presupposition that B did indeed say this.

decisions.claim: B is picking out a lipstick
decisions.reason: A's question 'How long does it take you to pick out a lipstick' directly presupposes B is picking out a lipstick. The question's structure requires this to be true for it to be meaningful.

decisions.claim: B is picking out some nail polish
decisions.reason: Same presupposition structure as c2: 'pick out a lipstick and some nail polish' presupposes B is picking out nail polish.

decisions.claim: B is buying a thirty-dollar item (referred to as a crayon by A)
decisions.reason: A says 'Get the stupid thirty dollar crayon!' — an imperative directed at B, presupposing B is in the process of buying/selecting this thirty-dollar item. The 'crayon' label is A's sarcastic description.

decisions.claim: B is shopping for cosmetics, specifically at least a lipstick and nail polish
decisions.reason: This is a compound restatement of c2 and c3 combined. It adds no new information beyond what c2 and c3 already establish individually.

decisions.claim: B previously stated they were only going to get a few things
decisions.reason: This is bidirectionally equivalent to c1 — same event (B's prior statement about getting a few things), same evidence, same granularity. c1 is the more concise canonical form.

decisions.claim: B has been shopping for approximately one hour
decisions.reason: A states 'We have been here for almost an hour' — the 'we' includes B, so B has been at the location for approximately one hour. This is a direct statement with B as a participant.

decisions.claim: B has gathered multiple items beyond what they originally said they would get
decisions.reason: Turn 7's 'all this' and 'each one of these little things' presupposes B has gathered multiple items. Combined with turn 5's 'you said you were only going to get a few things,' the contrast establishes B has exceeded their stated plan.
decisions.counterexample: B might have gathered multiple items that were all part of the original 'few things' plan, but A's frustration and the contrast language make this unlikely.

decisions.claim: B is at a store selling cosmetics/beauty products
decisions.reason: The combination of lipstick, nail polish, and the 'crayon' (likely a cosmetic pencil) strongly presupposes B is at a cosmetics/beauty store. A's 'We have been here' confirms B is at this location.

decisions.claim: One of the items B selected costs thirty dollars
decisions.reason: A explicitly states the item costs thirty dollars ('thirty dollar crayon'). This is a fact about the item B is selecting/buying.

decisions.claim: B redirected the outing from eating to shopping at a cosmetics store
decisions.reason: This infers B's agency in redirecting the outing. While A proposed eating in turn 1 and they ended up shopping, A's turn 3 'Will you take long?' could imply various scenarios. We cannot determine from A's turns alone whether B 'redirected' the outing or whether they agreed to shop together, or whether the shopping was always part of the plan alongside eating. This is an unsupported attribution of agency and motivation to B.
decisions.counterexample: They could have gone to eat first then shopped, or B could have suggested adding shopping to the plan, or they could have been shopping before eating was proposed.
